title: Low-dose Juglone Attenuates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy through Lys207-dependent FoxO1 activation and Mitochondrial protection.
authors: Hongyu Chen; Zhihao Yang; Cheng Zhang; Chengxin Ge; Yingliang Zhao; Shaopeng Cheng; Yilin Wang; Hao Chen; Can Xu; Dongjin Wang; Jie Yang
abstract: Pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and redox imbalance. Here, we investigated the efficacy, safety window, and redox-regulatory mechanism of juglone, a naturally occurring 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone. In mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC), high-dose juglone induced cardiac, hepatic, and renal toxicity, whereas 1mg/kg/day was well tolerated and attenuated cardiac hypertrophy. Juglone also suppressed Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure and mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP production, and redox homeostasis. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that juglone reduced stress-associated cardiomyocyte states and enriched calcium-handling cardiomyocytes. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, Biotin-Juglone pull-down assay, surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assays, molecular docking, and mutational analyses identified FoxO1 as a functional target of juglone. Juglone engaged the FoxO1 DNA-binding domain in a Lys207-dependent manner, and was associated with FoxO1 deacetylation, nuclear accumulation, and transcriptional activation. Activated FoxO1 induced Sesn3 transcription and restored AMPK phosphorylation at Thr172. Sesn3 silencing markedly attenuated juglone-induced AMPK activation and impaired its protective effects against cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. FoxO1 silencing, FoxO1-K207Q mutation, blockade of FoxO1 deacetylation, or inhibition of FoxO1 transcriptional activity impaired these benefits. Importantly, myocardium from patients with aortic valve stenosis-associated hypertrophy exhibited increased FoxO1 acetylation, reduced cardiomyocyte nuclear FoxO1 localization, decreased Sesn3 expression and AMPK phosphorylation, and increased 4-HNE. Collectively, low-dose juglone attenuates pathological hypertrophy and preserves mitochondrial homeostasis through the FoxO1-Sesn3-AMPK axis, while highlighting the importance of dose-dependent redox effects in determining its therapeutic efficacy and systemic toxicity.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
authors: Lytfi Krasniqi; Mohanad Hamandi; Poul Erik Mortensen; Henrik Nissen; Patricia A Pellikka; Barry A Borlaug; Oke Gerke; Amal Haujir; Louise Oeksnebjerg Krasniqi; Christian Juhl Terkelsen; Lars Peter Riber; Jordi Sanchez Dahl
abstract:
GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.
Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.
Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).
Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: Perioperative B-Cell-Targeted Therapy for High-Risk Valve Surgery in Active Primary Sjögren's Disease.
authors: Bing Li; Lili Pan; Hua Liao
abstract:
Primary Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by B-cell dysregulation. Clinically significant valvular involvement is uncommon, and evidence guiding perioperative immunomodulation remains limited.
A 59-year-old woman with SjD and severe aortic stenosis required valve replacement. Preoperative evaluation demonstrated active SjD with elevated inflammatory markers and hypergammaglobulinemia. Following multidisciplinary discussion, telitacicept, corticosteroids, and hydroxychloroquine were initiated before surgery. After improvement in inflammatory activity, the patient underwent aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement. Histopathologic examination showed degenerative valvular changes with focal inflammatory cell infiltration. The postoperative course was uneventful, with normal prosthetic valve function at 1-year follow-up.
This case highlights the challenges of managing severe valvular heart disease in patients with active primary SjD and a multidisciplinary perioperative strategy incorporating B-cell-targeted therapy. Although preoperative immunomodulation may have attenuated the histopathologic evidence of immune-mediated valvular involvement, the case offers insights when guidance is limited.

title: Intraoperative ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicating Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
authors: Xunlai Lu; Yuanjia Luo; Fanjing Wang; Wei Cao; Jing Cheng; Peng Lu; Shenrui Xu; Jiachao Luo
abstract:
Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction concurrent with endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm is an extremely rare and life-threatening emergency, currently lacking unified clinical guidelines for reference.
A 61-year-old male patient underwent endovascular aneurysm repair for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and experienced persistent hypotension during the procedure. Postprocedural electrocardiogram and cardiac enzyme tests confirmed acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The patient underwent emergency coronary angiography, which revealed severe stenosis, followed by successful balloon angioplasty. The patient recovered and was discharged following multidisciplinary postoperative care.
This case demonstrates the management principles for multiple life-threatening complications, where the clinical challenge formed by the huge retroperitoneal hematoma (bleeding risk) and the requirement for antiplatelet therapy after urgent revascularization (ischemic risk) was properly addressed. Through accurate identification, precise intervention, and multidisciplinary team collaboration, the patient was successfully rescued. This case provides a referable practical path for clinical decision-making in similar rare scenarios, highlighting the critical value of individualized treatment strategies.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
authors: Rafael Gonzalez-Manzanares; Soledad Ojeda; Ignacio Amat-Santos; Albert Ariza-Solé; Rafael Romaguera; Diego López Otero; Luis Nombela-Franco; Livia Gheorge; Jorge Sanz-Sánchez; Carlos Baladrón Zorita; Ignacio Gallo; Rafael Cobas Paz; Antonio Jesús Muñoz García; Victoria Vilalta; Gabriela Veiga Fernández; Juan Gabriel Córdoba Soriano; Pedro Cepas-Gillén; Miriam Sandín Rollán; Xacobe Flores Ríos; Ricardo Palma-Carbajal; Roberto Martín Reyes; Pablo Avanzas; Sergio García Blas; Juan A Franco-Peláez; Javier Martín Moreiras; José Ramón Gonzalez Juanatey; Nieves Gonzalo; German Calle; José Luis Díez; Sandra Santos-Martínez; Rocío González Ferreiro; Erika Muñoz García; Eduard Fernandez-Nofrerias; Xoan Sanmartín; Gabriela Tirado; Alejandro Gutierrez Barri; Inmaculada González Bermúdez; Xavier Rosselló; Valentín Fuster; Borja Ibáñez; Sergio Raposeiras Roubín
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.
In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.
Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.
Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Francesco Cardaioli; Luca Nai Fovino; Tommaso Fabris; Giulia Masiero; Andrea Panza; Massimo Napodano; Chiara Fraccaro; Francesco Putortì; Giuseppe Tarantini
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract:
Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity.
We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.
This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria.
A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak.
Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
authors: Inês Fortuna; Janete Santos; Paula Soeiro; Raquel Machado; Ana Oliveira; Jorge Pereira; Giuseppe Limongelli; Teresa Faria; Elisabete Martins; European Reference Network for Rare, Low-Prevalence, or Complex Diseases of the Heart (ERN GUARD-Heart)
abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusing on HCM while also considering ischemic, inflammatory, infiltrative, and other non-ischemic forms of cardiac remodelling. Particular attention is given to the relationship between myocardial FAPI uptake, CMR tissue characterization, ventricular function, circulating biomarkers, and calculated arrhythmic risk. Although initial studies support the complementary value of FAPI PET and CMR for characterizing active and established myocardial remodelling, the available evidence remains limited by small, predominantly single-centre cohorts, heterogeneous radiotracers and acquisition protocols, and the absence of validated quantitative thresholds or prospective outcome data. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether FAPI PET can provide incremental prognostic information or serve as a reproducible imaging biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response.

title: Structural Optimization and Fatigue Performance Evaluation of Balloon-Expandable Aortic Valve Stents.
authors: Tao Cai; Chaoqun Zhao; Gang Fang
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a critical therapy for aortic stenosis, but most existing valve stents are designed for Western patients, whose aortic root anatomy differs from Chinese patients characterized by smaller annulus diameters, heavier calcification, and a higher prevalence of bicuspid valves. To address this mismatch, we designed a balloon-expandable aortic valve stent tailored for Chinese patients and systematically evaluated its performance. Four structural schemes were considered; a diamond-hexagonal composite mesh was selected based on radial strength, expansion uniformity, anchoring stability, sealing, and coronary access. Material properties of MP35N were obtained via tensile tests, and finite element models simulated crimping, recoil, and expansion. Among three end-corner geometries, the U-shaped design showed superior mechanical behavior with lower stress/strain concentrations. For stents crimped to 6.5 mm, maximum equivalent stress ranged from 1030 to 1076 MPa and plastic strain from 0.221 to 0.259; upon expansion to 20-29 mm, stress reached 1417-1493 MPa and strain 0.447-0.544, with strain concentrated at the corner ends. Simulated recoil matched experimental results within 7% relative error. Accelerated fatigue testing (4 × 108 cycles) of the bare stents revealed no fractures, displacements, or surface damage. These findings demonstrate that the optimized bare stent structure exhibits good mechanical feasibility, durability, and improved anatomical compatibility for Chinese TAVI patients, providing a promising device solution for domestic clinical application.

title: Kidney Function Trajectories in Patients with and Without Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Single-Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Hirofumi Sakuma; Satoshi Kawaguchi; Yuya Kitani; Tatsuya Aonuma; Naoko Kawabata; Erika Saito; Akiho Minoshima; Shingo Kunioka; Hiroyuki Kamiya; Naoki Nakagawa
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may improve systemic hemodynamics and kidney perfusion; however, its effect on long-term kidney function remains unclear. We evaluated kidney function trajectories before and after TAVR in patients with and without chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) who underwent TAVR between June 2016 and December 2024. Overall, 314 eligible patients were classified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) as without CKD (≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with CKD (<60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Linear mixed-effects models estimated pre- and post-TAVR eGFR slopes, which were compared between groups after covariate adjustment. Results: Median follow-up was 2.0 years. Adjusted pre-TAVR eGFR slopes were -2.11 (95% confidence interval [CI], -3.34 to -0.89) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -2.83 (95% CI, -3.65 to -2.01) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD. The post-TAVR slopes were -4.02 (95% CI, -5.68 to -2.35) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -0.83 (95% CI, -2.04 to 0.39) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD, with a significant group difference of 3.19 (95% CI, 1.44 to 4.94) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.001). In patients with CKD, the post-TAVR slope improved relative to the pre-TAVR slope by 2.01 (95% CI, 0.51 to 3.50) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.01), whereas no significant change was observed in those without CKD. Conclusions: eGFR decline after TAVR was attenuated in patients with CKD compared with those without CKD, suggesting that kidney function may be preserved through hemodynamic improvement following TAVR.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Combined TAVR-PCI Versus SAVR-CABG in Patients with Aortic Stenosis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Ricardo Antonio Rodriguez Mejia; Mathhar Aldaoud; Ifeanyi Momodu; Merina Dongol; Girum Feyissa; Kelechi Aruogu; Zamaraq M Bhatti; Abdul Haseeb Riaz; Nafisa Saleem
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery disease coexists with severe aortic stenosis in about half of patients. Surgical aortic valve replacement with coronary artery bypass grafting (SAVR+CABG) is guideline-recommended, but transcatheter aortic valve replacement with percutaneous coronary intervention (TAVR+PCI) is increasingly used. Prior meta-analyses double-counted overlapping populations and did not report randomized evidence separately; we re-examined the comparison after correcting both. Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 for randomized and comparative observational studies, excluding reports with overlapping populations. Outcomes were pooled with random-effects models, stratified by study design, and re-analysed without administrative databases. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results: Fourteen studies were included (two randomized trials, nine cohorts, three administrative databases), comprising 154,892 patients (28,569 TAVR+PCI; 126,323 SAVR+CABG). TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early mortality (odds ratio (OR) 0.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.84) and less acute kidney injury (OR 0.34, 0.20-0.57), but greater pacemaker implantation (OR 2.18, 1.93-2.46) and major vascular complications (OR 3.38, 1.65-6.89). Stroke, myocardial infarction and one-year mortality (OR 0.80, 0.58-1.10) did not differ; bleeding results were inconsistent (I2 = 95%). Over 12-72 months, mortality was higher with TAVR+PCI (hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 1.28-1.49; nine observational studies), unchanged without the largest cohort. Administrative databases drove heterogeneity but not the direction of any early outcome. Certainty was moderate for pacemaker implantation and low or very low otherwise; randomized data were too limited to confirm these findings. Conclusions: In predominantly observational evidence, TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early risk but higher mortality over longer follow-up. This trade-off supports individualized Heart Team decisions rather than the superiority of either strategy. Adequately powered randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Complex Anatomy: An Anatomy-Driven Framework for Bicuspid Stenosis, Pure Aortic Regurgitation, and the Small Annulus in the Era of Lifetime Management.
authors: Daniel Miron Brie; Cristian Mornoș; Roxana Popescu; Alina Diduța Brie
abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is established for severe calcific tricuspid aortic stenosis, but its application in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) stenosis, pure native aortic regurgitation (AR), and small aortic annulus anatomy remains limited by heterogeneous morphology, device-specific constraints, and uncertain long-term outcomes. These settings require decisions that extend beyond immediate procedural success to encompass coronary access, reintervention, valve durability, and associated aortopathy. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes an anatomy-driven framework integrating imaging, device selection, procedural planning, and lifetime management. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from 1 January 2010 to 31 March 2026 for studies addressing TAVI in BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annulus anatomy. Randomized trials, meta-analyses, multicenter registries, pivotal device studies, and guideline or consensus documents were prioritized. After screening 2663 records and assessing 330 full-text reports, 101 records were retained for qualitative synthesis. Evidence was appraised by anatomical substrate, imaging phenotype, device strategy, procedural hazards, and implications for lifetime management. Results: In BAV stenosis, contemporary registry and prospective cohort data support high device success and acceptable early and mid-term outcomes in carefully selected patients; however, calcified raphe, bulky asymmetric leaflet or left ventricular outflow tract calcification, annular eccentricity, and concomitant aortopathy identify higher-risk phenotypes that often favor surgery. Randomized evidence in younger low-risk BAV patients remains limited and exploratory, with the NOTION-2 trial showing a numerically higher 3-year composite event rate after TAVI than surgical aortic valve replacement (20.4% vs. 7.8%; hazard ratio 2.9, 95% confidence interval 0.9-9.0) in the small bicuspid subgroup. In pure native AR, lack of annular calcification and frequent root dilatation impair anchoring of conventional transcatheter heart valves, increasing risks of migration, embolization, residual AR, and second-valve implantation. Dedicated leaflet-anchoring devices have improved outcomes: in ALIGN-AR, the JenaValve Trilogy system achieved procedural success above 95% in high-surgical-risk patients, although evidence remains single-arm and nonrandomized. In small annuli, the strongest comparative evidence comes from the SMART trial, in which supra-annular self-expanding valves were non-inferior to balloon-expandable valves for the 12-month clinical composite and reduced moderate/severe prosthesis-patient mismatch at 30 days (11.2% vs. 35.3%). Across all three phenotypes, electrocardiography-gated computed tomography is fundamental for defining anchoring, sizing, calcium distribution, root and coronary anatomy, anticipated coronary re-access, and the feasibility of redo-TAVI. Surgery remains particularly relevant when aortic repair, annular/root enlargement, or a more durable lifetime strategy is required. Conclusions: TAVI is feasible in selected patients with BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annuli, but the evidentiary strength and optimal procedural strategy differ substantially across these anatomies. Treatment should be guided by an anatomy-driven, computed-tomography-based Heart Team assessment that integrates immediate procedural feasibility with age, surgical candidacy, aortopathy, prosthesis-patient mismatch risk, coronary access, durability, and future reintervention options. Surgery remains the more established strategy for many younger, operable patients with unfavorable BAV morphology or aortopathy, AR with root dilatation, or very small annuli amenable to enlargement. Dedicated randomized trials, standardized imaging criteria, and long-term durability data are needed to refine lifetime management in complex aortic valve anatomy.

title: The Cusp-Overlap Technique Versus the Standard Three-Cusp Technique for Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valves-A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Alexandru Ispas; Damien Brunet; Redouane Saady; Yacoub Habib; Catalin Pestrea; Laurent Drogoul
abstract: Background: Conduction disturbances and the subsequent need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI) remain a major limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with self-expanding transcatheter heart valves (SE-THVs). The cusp-overlap technique (COT) has been proposed to optimize implantation depth and reduce PPMI rates compared to the standard three-cusp technique (3CT). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 113 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR with the Medtronic CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV(Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) between September 2020 and March 2023. Patients were treated using either COT (n = 49) or 3CT (n = 62). Baseline characteristics, procedural outcomes, and 30-day clinical events were compared before and after one-to-one propensity score matching. The primary endpoint was the incidence of PPMI at hospital discharge; the secondary endpoint was a composite of death, stroke, life-threatening or disabling bleeding, major vascular complications, and moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation at 30 days. A post hoc power calculation was performed given the low observed event rate. Results: Procedural success was achieved in 98.2% of patients. In the unmatched cohort, PPMI occurred in 6.1% (COT) vs. 9.7% (3CT) (p = 0.48). In the matched cohort (49 pairs), PPMI rates were 6.1% (COT) vs. 12.2% (3CT) (p = 0.48). With only 3 vs. 6 PPMI events in the matched cohort, the study had an estimated post hoc power of approximately 19% (two-sided α = 0.05) to detect the observed difference, so the negative primary result should be regarded as inconclusive rather than as evidence of equivalence between techniques. The secondary composite endpoint occurred less frequently in the COT group both before matching (14.3% vs. 32.3%; p = 0.049) and after matching (14.3% vs. 30.6%, p = 0.049). This composite difference was driven predominantly by the moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation (PVL) component (12.2% vs. 24.2% unmatched; 12.2% vs. 22.4% matched) rather than by death, stroke, or major vascular complications. Evolut device generation differed markedly by arm (COT patients received later-generation devices far more often than 3CT; p < 0.001), and is presented in the Methods/Results Sections as a key temporal confounder. COT was associated with a lower incidence of moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation, without prolonging procedural time. Conclusions: In this real-world single-center cohort, the cusp-overlap technique was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in PPMI after TAVR with the CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV. COT was, however, associated with fewer paravalvular leaks and a lower rate of the secondary composite of adverse clinical events at 30 days.

title: Lipoprotein(a): Particle vs mass and prevalent cardiovascular disease in the cardiovascular risk in Young Finns study population.
authors: Olli Raitakari; Matias Knuuti; Anna Linko-Parvinen; Katja Pahkala; Suvi Rovio; Noora Kartiosuo; Sini Stenbacka; Irina Lisinen; Britt-Marie Loo; Terho Lehtimäki; Mika Kähönen; Claudia Lamina; Florian Kronenberg; Markus Juonala; Jorma S A Viikari; Juha Mykkänen
abstract:
Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] can be reported as mass (mg/dL) or particle concentration (nmol/L). Because Lp(a) acts at the particle level, molar concentration may better reflect biologically relevant exposure.
To compare molar- and mass-based Lp(a) in relation to cardiovascular outcomes, risk classification, LPA genetic variation, and apo(a) isoform phenotype in the Young Finns Study.
Molar Lp(a) was measured using a traceable Roche Tina-quant Gen.2 assay and mass using a nontraceable Thermo Fisher assay. Associations with cardiovascular outcomes and aortic valve stenosis were assessed by logistic regression in adults aged ≥40 years (N = 3898). Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and guideline-based risk reclassification. Associations with LPA genetic risk score and apo(a) isoform phenotype were assessed using Spearman correlation.
Both metrics showed similar associations across cardiovascular outcomes, with significant associations for coronary artery disease (CAD) and aortic valve stenosis. In fully adjusted CAD models, the odds ratio for the highest vs lowest quintile was 1.55 for molar and 1.67 for mass. Agreement between guideline-based risk categories was 95.6%. Molar assigned 2.9% of individuals to a higher risk category than mass, vs 1.5% in the opposite direction. The molar-to-mass ratio was associated with LPA score and apo(a) isoform size, with greater attenuation after adjustment for molar than mass.
Molar and mass showed comparable associations with cardiovascular outcomes. However, molar reporting aligned more closely with the genetic and structural determinants of Lp(a) and more often assigned individuals to higher guideline-based risk categories, supporting continued standardization toward particle-based reporting.

title: Aspirin for primary prevention in patients with high lipoprotein(a): A promising therapeutic option while awaiting future therapies?
authors: Francesca Vittone; Giuliana Autiero; Sara Angela Malerba; Elisabetta Grolla; Michele Dalla Vestra
abstract: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor, linked to both atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma Lp(a) levels between 30-50mg/dL suggest a moderate risk, while levels of 51-180mg/dL indicate high risk, and concentrations exceeding 180mg/dL are linked to a very high cardiovascular risk. Currently, there are no approved therapies specifically indicated to lower Lp(a). Recent evidences indicate a role of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with high Lp(a). In this review, we discuss the results of the studies that explored the impact of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with increased Lp(a) while waiting for the results from large-scale research initiative exploring the impact of RNA-targeting Lp(a)-lowering therapies in reducing cardiovascular risk. In conclusion, waiting for the ongoing trials on emerging RNA-based therapies, the use of aspirin in a subgroup of patients with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk, with very high Lp(a) levels and without important bleeding risk could be an interesting strategy. Emerging RNA-targeted therapies might offer in future increased protection against the occurrence of major atherosclerotic cardiovascular events compared to standard lipid management agents in these patients.

title: Pelacarsen and Lp(a)HORIZON: Interpreting the Disconnect Between Lipoprotein(a) Lowering and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
authors: Pierre Sabouret; Domenico Mario Giamundo; Elad Asher; Salvatore De Rosa; Giuseppe Andò; Felice Gragnano; Roger S Blumenthal; Dan Atar; Mamas A Mamas
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Pelacarsen, a hepatocyte-directed antisense oligonucleotide targeting apolipoprotein(a), was evaluated in Lp(a)HORIZON, the first large phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial specifically designed to test whether pharmacological Lp(a) lowering reduces cardiovascular events. Topline results announced in September 2026 indicated that pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) but did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint in patients with established cardiovascular disease. Full trial data are awaited, and the mechanisms underlying this neutral result remain uncertain. We discuss potential explanations, including treatment after prolonged cumulative Lp(a) exposure, advanced vascular disease, intensive background prevention, the magnitude and duration of Lp(a) suppression, patient selection, baseline cardiovascular risk, and biological heterogeneity. We also examine implications for emerging therapies, including olpasiran, zerlasiran, lepodisiran, and muvalaplin, and for the design of ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Maethas Panyawongkhanti; Peerawat Chintrakulchai; Chonthicha Tanking; Wongsakorn Luangphiphat
abstract:
Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

title: Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Model Using Phonocardiogram and Single-Lead ECG Signals for Detecting Moderate-or-Greater Aortic Stenosis: Multicenter External Validation.
authors: Shumpei Saito; Masanobu Ishii; Shimpei Ogawa; Hiroshi Seki; Koshiro Ikeda; Youhei Kayano; Yuhei Yasui; Ginga Sato; Mitsuru Ohishi; Takuro Kubozono; Naritatsu Saito; Eri Toda Kato; Masahiro Yamada; Shunsuke Natori; Yuki Kunikane; Takafumi Yokomatsu; Masashi Kato; Yasuaki Sagara; Nami Uchiyama; Nobuhiko Atsuchi; Shota Kawahara; Shoji Natsugoe; Noriaki Tabata; Kenichi Tsujita
abstract:
Valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis (AS), often remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, making early detection challenging. Although cardiac auscultation is a traditional screening tool, its diagnostic accuracy is limited. We aimed to externally validate a deep learning-based model (eAS model) using phonocardiogram (PCG) and single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals to detect moderate-or-greater AS.
PCG and ECG recordings were acquired using a PCG device (Cardio-EGG). Transthoracic echocardiography served as the reference standard. The external validation cohort consisted of 951 patients from 3 medical institutions, including 70 with moderate-or-greater AS. The primary outcome was sensitivity for detecting moderate-or-greater AS; secondary outcomes included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios (LR).
The external validation cohort (n = 951, median age 73 years, male 65%) exhibited more advanced valvular disease than the training/development cohort. The eAS model achieved an AUROC of 0.9632 (95% CI: 0.9471-0.9774). Using the pre-determined threshold, sensitivity was 92.9% and specificity 87.9%, yielding a positive LR of 7.65 and negative LR of 0.08. Model-derived probabilities showed strong associations with echocardiographic measures of AS severity (adjusted R2 = 0.5051 for peak transvalvular velocity). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed generally consistent performance, although estimates were imprecise in small subgroups.
The eAS model demonstrated high diagnostic performance for detecting moderate-or-greater AS in a multicenter external validation cohort. AI-based PCG/ECG analysis may support the decision to refer patients from auscultation to echocardiography for AS evaluation.

title: Stent biomechanics in hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis: from site-specific loading to a staged device-validation framework.
authors: Shanyuan Jin; Chuhan Chen; Guiye Na; Lin Guo; Li Dai; Bing Liu
abstract: Hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis is usually managed as one local variant of central venous stenosis, yet its mechanical environment is distinctive. The vein follows a long, multi-axially curved retrosternal course through a narrow window between the manubrium and the aortic arch, bounded by two separate junctions, the lateral venous angle and the medial brachiocephalic-caval confluence. An implanted stent is therefore exposed to focal unidirectional compression, cyclic bending and torsion, short landing zones, and branch-coverage risk, conditions not reproduced by circumferential radial testing. The sternum-aortic corridor reported in affected patients, about 4.6 mm, is narrower than the nominal diameter of stents deployed there, placing the implied compression at or beyond the lowest level characterized in published bench comparisons; pulsatile durability testing covers only cardiac-frequency diametric cycling, and pooled cohorts seldom report the segment separately. This Review synthesizes published anatomical, clinical, engineering, and computational evidence and reframes the problem as a site-specific biomechanical and device-validation question with three validation priority stages (P1-P3). P1 (required) evaluates base-platform mechanics, structure, fatigue, and deployment: focal crush resistance and recovery, radial resistive versus chronic outward force, bending and torsion durability, foreshortening, deployment accuracy, branch preservation and, for covered constructs, covering fatigue. P2 (required) evaluates anatomy-specific hemodynamics of the same platform by patient-specific computational modeling and experimental flow testing, reporting shear, residence, gradient, edge-recirculation, branch-flow, and pressure-loss metrics against matched comparators. P3 (optional) covers an added drug, coating, or surface; baseline thrombogenicity, hemocompatibility, tissue compatibility, and structural integrity remain required base-platform attributes. We state two falsifiable hypotheses with the bench, computational, imaging, and clinical evidence that would support or refute them: H1 (mechanical), that resistance to focal unidirectional crush may govern stent deformation, durability, and in-stent restenosis localization more strongly than circumferential radial resistive force alone; and H2 (hemodynamic), that stent architecture and edge configuration may generate spatially reproducible disturbed-flow regions adding incremental prediction of later in-stent restenosis distribution beyond anatomical and procedural covariates. Direct prospective evidence remains sparse: the framework is a problem definition and validation roadmap, not a clinical algorithm, device ranking, or evidence of superior performance.

title: Modified balloon-assisted shoehorn technique for transcatheter aortic valve implantation in functionally horizontal anatomy: a case report.
authors: Nilkanth Patil; Rajeev Menon; Uday Kiran Anne; Pragathi Gurram; Anuj Kapadiya
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) poses unique challenges. We report a case in which an apparently benign anatomy resulted in failure of conventional delivery strategies and required a novel balloon-assisted bailout technique.
A 59-year-old man with a background history of liver cirrhosis presented with severe aortic stenosis due to type 1 BAV. The patient was in Child-Pugh class A with model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score of 14; hence, he was planned for TAVI in view of high surgical risk. Pre-procedural computed tomography showed a favourable left ventricular (LV)-aortic angle, but the fused non-coronary and right-coronary cusp behaved like functional horizontal anatomy. Various previously described wire and balloon-assisted techniques failed to deliver the valve. A novel balloon-assisted modified 'shoe-horn' technique, by inflating a 16 mm balloon in non-coronary sinus, altered the delivery trajectory and enabled successful valve delivery.
BAV with right non-coronary cusps fusion may behave like horizontal anatomy, despite favourable LV-aortic angle. A modified balloon-assisted shoe-horn technique can facilitate valve delivery when conventional methods fail. This case highlights an under-recognized mechanism of valve delivery failure in BAV and emphasizes the importance of preparedness for advanced bailout strategies.

title: Impaired Flow and Physiology in Coronaries With Anomalous Origin From the Opposite Sinus of Valsalva.
authors: Mauro Lo Rito; Mattia Squillace; Mauro Luca Agnifili; Antonio Rosato; Serena Anglese; Adele Chiavetta; Camilla Muritti; Miriam Deamici; Jessica Negri; Andrea Attanasio; Gianluigi Guida; Giandomenico Disabato; Francesco Secchi; Michele Conti; Alessandro Frigiola; Massimo Chessa; Alessandro Giamberti; Francesco Bedogni
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA) high-risk anatomical features (intramural segment, acute take-off angle, slit-like ostium) cause coronary stenosis leading to myocardial infarction. How these features alter coronary physiology remains unclear.
We aimed to evaluate their impact on coronary blood supply using continuous thermodilution.
We prospectively enrolled 51 AAOCA patients undergoing continuous thermodilution. Subjects were classified into an ischemic risk (IR) group (intramural segment, acute angle, oval or slit ostium) or non-ischemic risk (no-IR) group. Non-anomalous coronary arteries served as controls. We measured absolute coronary blood flow (CBF) and microvascular resistance.
Subjects (median age 48.4 years) presented mostly with angina, syncope, and arrhythmia. Final analysis included 48 AAOCA cases (31 IR, 17 no-IR) and 45 controls. The IR group had a median IM length of 9 mm, take-off angle of 31.9°, and a slit-like or oval ostium. The no-IR group had a median angle of 51.5° and an oval or round ostium. At rest, absolute CBF and microvascular resistance showed no significant differences among groups. However, during hyperemia, the IR group had significantly reduced CBF compared to controls (179 vs. 290 mL/min, p = 0.015). The IR group demonstrated higher microvascular resistance at rest (1473 vs. 1150, p = 0.024) and during hyperemia (433 vs. 305, p = 0.012), indicating persistently increased coronary vascular tone.
High-risk anatomical features of AAOCA are associated with altered coronary physiology. An intramural segment, acute take-off angle, and slit-like or oval ostium are linked to reduced hyperemic coronary blood flow due to increased microvascular resistance.

title: Liquid and solid layers in a thermal deep-learning machine.
authors: Gang Huang; Lai Shun Chan; Hajime Yoshino; Ge Zhang; Yuliang Jin
abstract: We study generalization in overparameterized deep neural networks using a thermal deep learning machine with a well-defined Hamiltonian. We find that learning dynamics organize the network into a solid-liquid-solid structure, where boundary layers are constrained while central layers remain flexible. These layers exhibit distinct dynamical behaviors, including timescale separation and nonequilibrium aging. We show that the solution space is structureless in liquid layers but hierarchically organized in solid layers, indicating a direct link between dynamics and landscape geometry. These results suggest a physical perspective for generalization, arising from the interplay between flexible representations and boundary-induced constraints.

title: The adoption, efficacy, and limitations of large language models in urological education: A cross-sectional survey.
authors: Wesam Khan
abstract: The integration of large language models into medical education is rapidly transforming pedagogical approaches, particularly in specialized fields like urology. This study aims to evaluate the adoption patterns, perceived efficacy, and significant limitations of these artificial intelligence (AI) tools among urology trainees. This research employed a descriptive, cross-sectional study design through an online survey disseminated to urology trainees at a single institution. A total of 194 complete responses were collected from medical students and interns. The survey assessed adoption patterns, perceived efficacy on a 7-point Likert-scale, and limitations. The analysis revealed near-universal adoption (98.4%), with 65% of participants using AI tools daily, predominantly ChatGPT. Key applications included generating exam-style questions and summarizing complex guidelines. Participants reported significant perceived improvements in core knowledge areas, with the highest gains in disease knowledge and diagnostics (Median = 7, interquartile range: 6-7), which were strongly correlated with increased clinical confidence. Multivariate regression identified usage frequency and comfort with technology as significant predictors of knowledge improvement (β = 0.29, P = .001) and confidence gains (β = 0.30, P < .001). The primary limitation identified was the potential for AI "hallucinations" or incorrect information (54.1%). Large language models are widely adopted and perceived as highly effective for enhancing knowledge and clinical reasoning in urological education. However, their transformative potential is tempered by critical concerns regarding reliability. A balanced approach that combines these powerful AI tools with vigilant oversight is essential.

title: Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears: A systematic review from image optimization to prognosis prediction.
authors: Haitao Wang; Deming Guo; Yingqi Gao; Weixin Xian; Liyan Zhang
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway.
We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically.
Sixty-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised-phenotyping study. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data. QUADAS-2 classified overall risk-of-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction-model studies as high risk-of-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference.
AI has proof-of-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and standardized task-specific reporting are required.

title: Comparative evaluation of AI-driven large language models for periodontal-orthodontic patient questions: accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, and temporal consistency.
authors: Resül Çolak; Merve Küçükoğlu Çolak; Orhan Cicek
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to provide patient-oriented oral health information; however, their performance in answering periodontal-orthodontic patient questions remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the performance of contemporary AI-driven LLMs in answering periodontal-orthodontic patient questions by assessing response accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, and temporal consistency.
Thirty patient-oriented periodontal-orthodontic questions were submitted to six contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT 5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek 3.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4.20, and PerioGPT) under standardized conditions, and the generated responses were analyzed. Accuracy and comprehensiveness were evaluated using a modified five-point Likert scale, whereas readability was assessed using the Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) indices. Temporal consistency was assessed by repeating the response-generation process one week later. Inter-model comparisons and temporal consistency analyses were performed using repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, as appropriate.
Significant differences were observed among the evaluated LLMs in accuracy (p < 0.001, Kendall's W = 0.401), comprehensiveness (p < 0.001, Kendall's W = 0.575), FRE (p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.807), and FKGL (p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.688). PerioGPT and Gemini achieved the highest accuracy (4.93 ± 0.13 and 4.90 ± 0.19, respectively) and comprehensiveness scores (4.85 ± 0.21 and 4.90 ± 0.22, respectively). PerioGPT generated highly accurate and comprehensive responses but exhibited the lowest FRE (12.7 ± 10.2) and highest FKGL (15.1 ± 2.1) scores, whereas Claude, DeepSeek, and Grok produced more readable outputs. Although some significant differences in temporal consistency were observed among the evaluated models, the associated effect sizes were generally small (0.041-0.143), indicating broadly similar performance over time.
While PerioGPT and Gemini achieved the highest accuracy and comprehensiveness scores, and Claude, DeepSeek, and Grok produced more readable responses, the evaluated models generally demonstrated similar temporal consistency over time; however, no model consistently outperformed the others across all evaluated criteria. Therefore, AI-driven LLMs may support patient education and oral health literacy in periodontal-orthodontic care; however, their use as complementary tools under expert supervision is recommended.

title: A topic-based framework for interpretable and sparse semantic representations.
authors: Ming Song; Qing Cai
abstract: In computational approaches to language, semantic representations produced by modern deep learning systems are often encoded as high-dimensional latent vectors that are difficult to interpret. By contrast, cognitive science has emphasized the need for semantic representations with interpretable and cognitively meaningful structures. Although researchers have explored concept representations using corpus-driven distributed embeddings and various feature-based paradigms, a scalable and interpretable framework that can represent linguistic materials across different levels of granularity remains an open methodological challenge. Recent advances in pretrained language models have led to topic modeling methods that leverage these models, such as BERTopic, which uses sentence-level embeddings to derive clusters corresponding to human-interpretable topics. Building on this line of work, the present study introduces a framework, SISTR, for representing Semantics as Interpretable and Sparse Topic-based Representations. The framework extracts interpretable topics from the corpus and models the semantics of linguistic materials via their relations to the derived topics. This framework is designed to accommodate linguistic materials across different levels and languages. We evaluated the interpretability of the resulting topic dimensions through behavioral experiments. We applied this framework to word association tasks and semantic judgments, comparing model predictions with human behavioral data. The results suggest that SISTR achieves competitive performance to existing semantic representation methods while providing sparse and interpretable semantic representations. Overall, SISTR provides a reusable semantic coordinate system that offers an interpretable bridge between linguistic data and cognitive theories of semantic representation.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Accurate lncRNA-Protein Interaction Prediction via Multi-Kernel Graph Embeddings and Self-Attention.
authors: Shivani Saxena; Ahsan Z Rizvi
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play a pivotal role in regulating biological processes, primarily through lncRNA-Protein Interactions (LPI), which are crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and cellular functions. While computational methods exist for predicting LPI, they suffer from suboptimal feature integration, limited generalizability, and inadequate network modeling. To address these challenges, we propose MAKGLPIN (Multi-Architecture, Multi-Kernel Graph-based LPI Network), a novel deep learning framework that integrates sequence features, structural information, and physicochemical properties of lncRNAs and proteins. MAKGLPIN employs a multi-layer Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) enhanced with a self-attention mechanism to capture complex interaction patterns, alongside a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to prioritize critical interactions while preserving long-range dependencies. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that MAKGLPIN outperforms existing methods in robustness, generalizability, and predictive precision across benchmark datasets. Our model provides a computationally efficient and biologically interpretable solution, advancing the study of LPI and their applications in disease research.

title: A Survey of Computational Color Constancy: Approaches and Emerging Applications in Medical Imaging.
authors: Achraf Tahar; Hadil Zrour; Agnieszka Pozdzik; Stéphane Dupont
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: As the evening sets in and natural light fades to artificial light, it is remarkable how the colors around us still appear nearly the same. This phenomenon, known as color constancy, allows us to perceive relatively stable colors even as lighting conditions change. In the field of computer vision, replicating this human ability is the key to performing tasks such as recognizing objects and understanding scenes. This review examines two main approaches to tackle the challenge of computational color constancy: traditional static methods that rely on a set of assumptions about lighting and scene conditions, and newer learning-based methods that use models trained to estimate lighting directly from images. We look at how these techniques have evolved, from foundational methods like the gray-world assumption, which work within certain limitations, to modern deep learning techniques that can interpret lighting in more dynamic ways. The datasets, metrics, and reported results of the surveyed studies are consolidated into two comparative tables, providing a structured overview of the methods discussed. Together, these comparisons offer a broad perspective on how computational color constancy has developed and where it is headed, with particular emphasis on its applications in medical imaging.

title: Investigation on Automatic Classification of Bone, Lymph Node, and Local Lesions in CT Images of Prostate Cancer Patients.
authors: Oona Rainio; Ahti Vehmanen; Anting Li; Maria K Jaakkola; Jukka Kemppainen; Riku Klén
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning. Following a computed tomography (CT) or a positron emission tomography (PET)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning (ML) and deep learning models. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of   18  F-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96.0%. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97.9±1.2%, 95.2±1.3%, and 93.1±2.8% in the five-fold cross-validation experiments of the primary data and 96.3%, 94.0%, and 80.0% on the external test set, respectively. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories.

title: Evaluating Explicit Anatomical Priors Beyond a Mature CT Detector for Six Acute Abdominal Emergencies.
authors: Hasan Mete Erdoğan; Ural Koç
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: To test whether anatomical priors from a general-purpose organ segmentation model (TotalSegmentator, TS), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language-model report labels; a nested 280-study radiologist-adjudicated subset was the reference standard. TS-derived slice selection (Arm A), organ-state integration (Arm B), and their combination (Arm C) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine-tuned conditions. The detector was also retrained from scratch (identical 10-epoch budget) with image channels only, with the patient's TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient's maps. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study-level bootstrap. The detector generalized externally (macro AUROC 0.816 cohort; 0.879 adjudicated). Slice selection was non-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ's axial range; organ-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis (hypothesis-generating). In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0.5 (0.517 versus 0.482), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve (0.822 versus 0.829; Δ -0.007, 95% CI -0.019 to +0.007) and kidney-stone AUROC fell (0.678 versus 0.768; exploratory), unlike with another patient's maps. Per-site recalibration was the most effective operating-point adjustment (macro F1 +0.021); annotation-free fine-tuning reduced discrimination. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector's overall external discrimination. Per-site recalibration gave the largest operating-point gain.

title: From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies.
authors: Yubing Zhou; Yunxiao Ge; Kangdong Liu; Hui Liu; Zigang Dong
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.

title: The Sound of Hypnotherapy: Identification of Paralinguistic Speech Features Using Acoustic Analysis and Deep Learning.
authors: Albin Grataloup; Angélique Remacle
journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
abstract: Hypnosis is an altered state of consciousness characterized by focused attention and heightened suggestibility, with therapeutic applications in a range of mental and somatic conditions. While prior research has emphasized the linguistic content of hypnotic suggestions (ie, what is said), the paralinguistic and acoustic characteristics of the hypnotist's speech (ie, how it is said) remain underexplored. This study investigated condition-associated paralinguistic characteristics in recordings of 32 hypnotherapists across hypnosis and control conditions, during both reading and spontaneous tasks. We first applied classical acoustic analysis using Praat to examine common temporal, energy, frequency, and spectral parameters of connected speech on the entire recordings. The findings identify a paralinguistic profile within this sample characterized by a lower proportion of voicing, reduced intensity, and decreased spectral energy at low frequencies in the hypnosis condition. We then employed deep learning techniques, training classifiers on both handcrafted acoustic features and mel spectrograms. Within the present dataset and for therapists represented during training, the models reliably distinguished 12-second speech segments from hypnosis and control conditions, with fundamental frequency and formant-related features (F0 and F1-F3) emerging as key predictors. Spectrogram-based models achieved higher performance, suggesting that additional acoustic cues contribute to classification under the present recording protocol.

title: A practical AI model for endoscopic diagnosis of gastric premalignant lesions and its application to predicting metachronous recurrence.
authors: Jinju Choi; Cheol Min Shin; Jinbae Park; Gyuseon Song; Jaeyoung Lee; Hae Dong Lee; Yong Hoon Choi; Soo-Jeong Cho; Seung Joo Kang; Young Soo Park; Nayoung Kim
journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
abstract:
To evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based optical system for chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) and intestinal metaplasia (IM), and its ability to predict metachronous recurrence.
We analyzed 72,794 endoscopic images from 5,000 patients undergoing esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsy-confirmed CAG/IM. A convolutional neural network model was developed and compared with experts (n=16) and novices (n=15). The association between AI-predicted IM extent and metachronous recurrence after endoscopic resection of early gastric cancer (n=458) was evaluated using Cox regression.
For CAG, the AI model achieved accuracies of 0.819 (antrum) and 0.864 (body), with corresponding AUCs of 0.885 and 0.901. For IM, accuracies were 0.759 and 0.723, with AUCs of 0.835 and 0.744. The AI model outperformed novices and experts in CAG diagnosis (accuracy: 0.855 vs. 0.705 and 0.751) and outperformed novices in IM diagnosis (0.875 vs. 0.781). Although individual HRs for AI-predicted IM extent were not statistically significant (2.11 [95% CI, 0.25-17.67], antral IM only; 4.27 [0.57-31.97], IM extending to body), a significant dose-response relationship with recurrence risk was observed (Ptrend=0.043).
This AI model showed clinically acceptable performance and potential usefulness for CAG/IM diagnosis in a single-center study but requires multicenter external validation before clinical adoption.

title: Robustness of Nomogram Versus Deep Learning Models for Hepatocarcinoma Grading: Insights From a Bilateral Cross-Center Validation.
authors: Zhijin Zhao; Weibin Zhang; Yuli Zhu; Qihui Guo; Qi Zhang; Hong Ding
abstract:
This study aimed to compare the performance of nomograms and deep learning (DL) models in predicting the pre-operative pathological grade of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) using clinical data and ultrasound images, with an emphasis on model robustness and generalizability across institutions.
We retrospectively analyzed 2404 pre-operative ultrasound images from 601 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC across two medical centers. Two distinct modeling strategies were employed: two nomograms integrating ultrasound imaging features (B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound [CEUS]) with clinical variables, and a series of DL models based on B-mode, CEUS at arterial phases, portal phases and delayed phases, and a combined B + CEUS modality. Independent predictors of pathological grade were identified using univariate, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator and logistic regression and incorporated into the nomograms. To rigorously assess generalizability, bilateral training and a cross-center validation strategy were implemented: data from Center 1 were split 7:3 for training and internal validation, while all data from Center 2 served as an external test set. This process was reversed (i.e., training on Center 2 and testing on Center 1) to complete the bilateral cross-center validation. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis.
The nomograms demonstrated strong and consistent performance in predicting HCC pathological grade, with AUCs of 0.771 (internal validation) and 0.762 (external validation) when trained on Center 1 data, and AUCs of 0.814 (internal) and 0.818 (external) when trained on Center 2 data. In contrast, DL models showed high internal performance (AUCs: 0.632-0.809 for Center 1; 0.692-0.767 for Center 2) but experienced significant degradation on external validation (AUCs: 0.599-0.646 and 0.620-0.657, respectively).
The nomogram exhibited superior robustness and generalizability compared to DL models in heterogeneous clinical populations. These findings highlight the practical advantage of interpretable statistical models in settings with variable data distributions and reinforce the value of feature-based approaches when data diversity is limited.

title: Decoding in-situ plant stress physiology via bio-hydrogel microneedles.
authors: Jun Fu; Tingting Zhang; Haorong Liao; Wenzhen Wang; Zhengrong Chen; Guohong Liu; Xiangzeng Kong; Qichang Hu
abstract: Electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) dynamics enables early monitoring of plant stress physiology, which is crucial for crop health management and yield optimization. However, invasive sensors damage plant tissues, whereas existing non-invasive approaches suffer from cuticular barriers and insufficient exploitation of dynamic biochemical signals, leading to high interfacial impedance, delayed responses, and low accuracy. Here, we introduce an integrated sensing and machine-learning framework (CRH-BMIS) that combines a highly specific Cs/rGO/HRP biohydrogel microneedle with algorithmic analytics. This system overcomes traditional barriers to in situ, tissue-level monitoring of abiotic and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000) stresses. By significantly lowering interfacial impedance, the microneedle exhibits a stable log-linear response over an ultra-broad range (0.01-8000 μM) with exceptional sensitivity (up to 12.46 μA cm-2 decade-1, LOD 0.00109 μM) and robust anti-interference. Furthermore, utilizing an intelligent diagnostic model based on stress-evoked H2O2 dynamics, CRH-BMIS achieves competitive cross-plant classification of abiotic/biotic stress (96.97% accuracy) and disease-stage classification (91.47% accuracy). This superior performance stems from the deep synergy between minimally invasive microneedles and machine learning algorithms. CRH-BMIS not only delivers accurate, generalizable in situ stress diagnosis but also enables scalable early-warning decision support.

title: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.
authors: Mei Tian; Lanzhi Wang; Turghun Muhammad; Jika Yang; Tajiguli Yimamumaimaiti; Dengbin Yu; Yan He; Zhiming Li
abstract:
Rapid and accurate analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar (CT) is essential yet challenging due to spectral overlap and matrix effects. Excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectral analysis using deep learning algorithms can address this challenge.
Coal tar samples were extracted and diluted with cyclohexane. A dataset of 1173 EEM spectra covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and various concentration gradients was constructed. Seven machine learning algorithms were used for qualitative classification of PAHs, and the deep learning algorithm, ResNet18, achieved the highest accuracy, close to 90%. Quantitative analysis was performed using a convolutional neural network-based variational autoencoder (CNN-VAE) model, yielding Root mean square error (RMSE) and (Mean absolute error) MAE values as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate PAH quantification in complex coal-tar matrices.
This new approach provides a cost-effective, rapid, and reliable alternative to conventional methods, mitigating issues such as Rayleigh scattering and spectral overlap. It offers a new strategy for detecting PAH molecules in complex matrices.

title: Why choose between prediction power and mechanistic insight in QSRR modeling? A case study of artificial membrane chromatography and machine learning.
authors: Wiktor Nisterenko; Julia Nicman; Jiayin Deng; Yash Raj Singh; Alicja Różycka; Katarzyna Ewa Greber; Daniel Szulczyk; Michał Nowacki; Maciej Dawidowski; Anna Drabczyk; Jolanta Jaśkowska; Przemysław Zaręba; Damian Kułaga; Marek Staszewski; Monika Wujec; Piotr Krzeczyński; Olga Michalak; Greta Klejborowska; Camilla Scarpellini; Koen Augustyns; Jaka Dernovšek; Tihomir Tomašič; Jan Korabecny; Joanna Fedorowicz; Jarosław Sączewski; Wiesław Sawicki; Defang Ouyang; Krzesimir Ciura
abstract: Quantitative structure-retention relationship (QSRR) modeling of immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was performed on a chemically diverse set of 2003 analytes to determine whether mechanistically interpretable, descriptor-based models can match the predictive performance of advanced machine-learning approaches. Chromatographic hydrophobicity indices (CHIIAM) were measured under standardized fast-gradient IAM conditions and modeled using three molecular representation strategies: physicochemical descriptors, ECFP4 fingerprints, and a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) operating on molecular graphs. Among the descriptor- and fingerprint-based methods, the Gradient Boosting Regressor gave the best performance. The descriptor-based model achieved a test R2 of 0.817, MAE of 4.43, and RMSE of 6.46 CHIIAM units, whereas the GIN model showed only a marginal numerical improvement (R2 = 0.828, MAE = 4.27, RMSE = 6.25). In contrast, fingerprint-based modeling performed worse (R2 = 0.771, MAE = 5.04, RMSE = 7.22). Statistical analysis of paired prediction errors showed no significant difference between the descriptor-based and GIN models, while the fingerprint-based model was the least accurate of the three. The observed differences among the best models were smaller than the long-term reproducibility of the IAM protocol. Applicability-domain analysis further showed that approximately 94-99% of compounds fell within the interpolation region. SHAP analysis identified lipophilicity, ionization, charge, and polarity as the major determinants of IAM retention, with cationic character enhancing retention and high polarity reducing it. These results demonstrate that descriptor-based QSRR modeling can achieve near-deep learning performance while preserving mechanistic interpretability, providing a practical and physically grounded strategy for IAM retention prediction.

title: Spatiotemporal deep learning with visualization predicts fertilization for early rescue intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
authors: Masato Saito; Hirofumi Haraguchi; Naoko Yamamoto; Shinya Fukuda; Kaori Shinya; Norio Masuya; Kazunori Matsumoto; Tomoki Tanaka; Yuya Yoshikawa; Satoshi Kishigami; Leona Matsumoto
abstract:
