To determine whether a deep learning (DL) model trained on time-lapse videos predicts fertilization following short-term insemination more accurately than senior embryologists, particularly in morphologically difficult cases, to visualize classification regions, and to evaluate whether a shortened observation window could still support accurate classification before early rescue intracytoplasmic sperm injection (r-ICSI).
Single-center retrospective study.
A total of 1,331 embryos from 250 short-term insemination cycles were identified. After excluding immature and degenerated oocytes, 1,016 embryos (770 fertilized, 246 unfertilized) were analyzed and split at the patient level into training and validation (n = 925) and test (n = 91) sets.
Time-lapse videos recorded from 4.5 to 8 h post-insemination were input into a spatiotemporal convolutional neural network trained with 5-fold cross-validation and compared with independent classification by 5 senior embryologists (>5 years' experience). Holdout embryos were stratified by embryologist accuracy, and classification regions were visualized. Model performance was also assessed using progressively truncated videos.
Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), accuracy, recall, specificity, precision, negative predictive value (NPV), and F1 score on the holdout test set, and stratum-specific accuracy.
The DL model achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.938 (ensemble model, 0.968) and significantly higher accuracy (0.884 versus 0.802), recall (0.946 versus 0.837), NPV (0.802 versus 0.557), and F1 score (0.927 versus 0.867) than senior embryologists. In moderate- and low-accuracy cases (≤3 of 5 embryologists correct), the DL model classified fertilized embryos significantly more accurately than embryologists (P < 0.05). Even when trained on videos truncated at 6 h, recall and NPV remained significantly higher than embryologists using the full 4.5-8.0 h videos. Visualization showed cytoplasmic highlighting in fertilized embryos and polar body and perivitelline space highlighting in unfertilized embryos.
A DL model with region visualization achieved significantly higher predictive accuracy than senior embryologists, including for fertilized embryos in cases prone to human misclassification, and retained higher recall and NPV even when trained on videos truncated at 6 h. This suggests potential utility for early r-ICSI, although multicenter prospective validation is required.

title: Revealing Spatiotemporal NOx Emission Dynamics in the Yangtze River Delta Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks and TROPOMI Observations.
authors: Qin He; Kai Qin; Hongrui Gao; Man Sing Wong; Jason Blake Cohen
abstract: Accurate estimation of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for characterizing their impacts on atmospheric environment and supporting air pollution management. This study introduces an innovative inversion framework based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), designed to derive NOx emissions from TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) satellite observations. By embedding the physical laws governing atmospheric processes, this method effectively bridges traditional data assimilation techniques with the computational efficiency of deep learning. Unlike purely data-driven models, it directly integrates physical constraints from atmospheric mass continuity equation into the model training process, thereby avoiding the computational burden associated with chemical transport models (CTMs) and removing the need for CTM simulations for supervision. Application to the Yangtze River Delta region in China (2018-2023) revealed clear spatiotemporal variations in NOx emissions, capturing the reduction during the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent recovery. Emission uncertainties were quantified using Monte Carlo dropout, providing robust error estimates alongside the inversion results. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient and physically grounded basis for NOx emission inversion, with broad applicability to air quality assessment and environmental management.

title: Augmenting electronic health records for adverse event detection.
authors: Gün Kaynar; Zhaoyi You; Richard D Boyce; Takahiro Yakoh; Carl Kingsford
abstract:
Adverse events (AEs) resulting from medical interventions are significant contributors to patient morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Detection of these events using electronic health records (EHRs) can facilitate timely clinical interventions. However, effective detection remains challenging due to severe class imbalance, missing labels, and the complexity of EHR records. Classical machine learning approaches frequently underperform due to insufficient representation of minority adverse event classes and limited capacity to capture interactions among patient demographics, administered medications, and associated complications. This study aims to develop and evaluate a lightweight, NLP-inspired data augmentation framework for structured EHR data that improves minority-class adverse event detection without requiring complex generative models or pre-trained clinical language models.
We introduce TASER-AE (Tokenized Augmentation for Structured EHR-Adverse Events), a novel data augmentation pipeline tailored for structured EHR data, coupled with transformer-based classification. TASER-AE addresses these issues through an NLP-inspired data augmentation framework adapted for EHR, enabling effective minority-class representation in sparse and imbalanced clinical datasets. The augmented records produced by TASER-AE alleviate class imbalance by enriching the representation of minority adverse event classes, which enhances the robustness and predictive performance of the classifier.
TASER-AE yields minority-class F1 scores up to 0.67, substantially surpassing classical machine-learning baselines and generative augmentation, and consistently improving on prior edit-based augmentation methods, across multiple adverse event tasks. Experiments conducted on two distinct EHR datasets confirm TASER-AE's ability to substantially improve adverse event detection.
These results demonstrate the potential of structured, NLP-inspired augmentation methods to overcome data limitations in clinical predictive modeling, ultimately contributing to improved patient safety outcomes. TASER-AE is available at https://github.com/Kingsford-Group/taserae.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the choroidal challenge: A comprehensive review of AI applications in choroidal imaging.
authors: Oscar Matteo Gagliardi; Jay Chhablani; Marco Lupidi; Maria Carmela Saturno; Alessandro Lambiase; Danilo Iannetta
abstract: The choroid is a densely vascular layer that sustains the outer retina and may reflect systemic microvascular health. With the advent of new imaging techniques, choroidal imaging has become increasingly detailed, generating vast data volumes. Conventional analytic tools often fall short in managing these high-dimensional datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) automatically enhances, segments, and analyzes choroidal images, facilitating the discovery of choroidal biomarkers relevant to ocular and systemic disease. Yet, anatomical complexity, heterogeneous protocols, and a lack of large, annotated datasets hinder AI adoption. Overcoming these barriers is essential to assess AI-derived choroidal biomarkers as reliable diagnostic and prognostic tools.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

journal: Научный журнал "Вестник Актюбинского регионального университета имени К. Жубанова"
abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Predictors of Early Mortality After Open Aorto-Iliac Reconstruction in Patients with Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: An Observational Cohort Study
authors: Merei Imanbayev; Altay Dyussupov; Bekzhigit Tussupkanov; Ergali Muratzhanov; Ardak Mautbekova; Dinara Kozubayeva; Rustam Mukhametkhanov; Rail Gafurov; Nurbek Irgebayev; Dainius Pavalkis; Evgeniy Zhuravlev; Yersyn Sabitov
abstract: Background and Objectives: Open aorto-iliac reconstruction (AIR) for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD) remains a high-risk procedure due to multifocal atherosclerosis affecting coronary, cerebrovascular, and renal arterial beds. This study aimed to identify factors independently associated with 30-day mortality and explore factors associated with late mortality during available follow-up among 30-day survivors following open AIR. Materials and Methods: An observational, non-randomised cohort of 170 consecutive patients undergoing open AIR for AIOD between January 2018 and December 2024 was analysed. Univariate logistic regression was performed for 30-day mortality; given the limited number of events (n = 16), the primary multivariable analysis used penalized likelihood logistic regression (Firth correction). Late survival among 30-day survivors (landmark cohort, n = 154) was analysed using Kaplan–Meier methods and exploratory univariate Cox proportional hazards regression, with surviving patients censored at the last available follow-up; multivariable Cox modelling was not performed due to the limited number of late events (n = 10). Results: Thirty-day mortality was 9.4% (16/170) in the overall cohort. In the primary Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression, factors associated with 30-day mortality were: severe left IIA stenosis ≥ 70% (OR 9.68; 95% CI 3.08–30.43; p = 0.0001), chronic kidney disease (OR 3.62; 95% CI 1.03–12.66; p = 0.044), and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration, analysed continuously (OR 1.022 per minute; 95% CI 1.000–1.045); a conventional ≥60 min categorical threshold showed a consistent secondary association (OR 4.15; 95% CI 1.28–13.46; p = 0.018). Non-inclusion of IIA was associated with increased 30-day mortality on univariate analysis (OR 4.80; 95% CI 1.31–17.62; p = 0.018). Among the 154 patients entering the 30-day landmark cohort, 10 late deaths were observed during available follow-up. In exploratory univariate Cox regression, intraoperative blood loss was the only statistically significant factor associated with late mortality (HR 1.07 per 100 mL; 95% CI 1.03–1.12; p = 0.0006). Conclusions: Severe IIA disease, chronic kidney disease, and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration (analysed continuously) were independently associated with increased 30-day mortality after open AIR. Intraoperative blood loss was associated with late mortality in exploratory univariate survival analysis. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts with longer and more uniform follow-up.

title: Coronary Artery Disease among Patients Undergoing Valve Replacement Surgery: A Retrospective Study of Angiographic Profiles and Predictors at a Southern Indian Tertiary Care Centre
authors: Gailin Bronson Sebastian; Yokesh Madhavan; Venkatesh Babu; Kiron Sukulal; Jai Arthe; Arya Rajesh; Shreya Gailin; Krishna Viju
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
abstract: Introduction: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) frequently co-exists with Valvular Heart Disease (VHD). In developing countries like India, the shifting epidemiology from rheumatic to degenerative VHD alters this association. Concomitant CAD drastically dictates surgical strategies, yet local angiographic profile data remains scarce. Aim: To determine the angiographic profile and clinical predictors of CAD in patients undergoing Coronary Angiography (CAG) prior to valve replacement surgery at an Indian tertiary care centre. Materials and Methods: The present retrospective study was conducted at Sree Mookambika Institute of Medical Sciences, Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, South India, and analysed data of 200 consecutive patients undergoing preoperative CAG before valve replacement surgery. Demographic profiles, cardiovascular risk factors, echocardiographic parameters, and angiographic findings were reviewed. Patients were stratified into CAD and non CAD cohorts. Obstructive CAD was defined angiographically. Statistical analysis utilised Chi-square and Student’s t-tests. Results: The cohort’s mean age was 55.6±9.3 years; 127 (63.5%) were males (63.5%). Prevalences of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, and tobacco use were 71 (35.5%), 64 (32%), 30 (15%), and 15 (7.5%), respectively. Patients with CAD were significantly older (mean age: 59.2±8.5 vs 53.8±9.1 years; p<0.001) and predominantly males (72 (73.5%) vs. 55 (53.9%); p=0.005). Increasing age and diabetes mellitus emerged as independent predictors of CAD in multivariate analysis (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.05-1.13; p<0.001 and OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.10-5.63; p=0.028, respectively). No statistically significant association was observed between CAD status and valves involved namely, Mitral Valve Disease (MVD), Aortic Valve Disease (AVD) and combined valve disease or valve surgery performed. AVD showed a non significant trend toward higher prevalence in the CAD group (p=0.11). Left Anterior Descending (LAD) artery was the most frequently diseased vessel {49 (50%)}. Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was marginally lower in the CAD arm (54.2±12.4% vs 57.1±11.3%; p=0.05), while Atrial Fibrillation (AF) lacked statistical correlation (p=0.89). Conclusion: The CAD in Indian valve replacement candidates was independently associated with advanced age, diabetes mellitus, and standard atherosclerotic risk factors. There was no statistically significant association between presence of CAD and the underlying valve pathology, or the type of surgery performed. Preoperative angiographic screening is critical for precise surgical planning, which should be dictated not only by age but by the presence of cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Anesthesia Management in Pregnant Women with Cardiac Disease: A Narrative Review
authors: Berrin Günaydın; Nuray Camgöz Eryılmaz; Gözde İnan
abstract: This review addresses the perspective of an obstetric anesthesiologist, focusing on the practical principles of peripartum anesthetic management by integrating current evidence with contemporary guideline recommendations rather than providing a comprehensive overview of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy. It also provides a clinically oriented approach to hemodynamic optimization, delivery planning, neuraxial and general anesthetic management, and the treatment of obstetric cardiac emergencies. Ultimately, this review aims to answer the question every anesthesiologist faces in daily practice: “What should the anaesthesiologist do for cardiac pregnant patient?” Cite this article as: Gunaydin DB, Camgoz Eryilmaz N, Inan G. Anesthesia management in pregnant women with cardiac disease: a narrative review. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1693, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.261693.

title: Inflammatory Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm of Probable Autoimmune Etiology: A Case Report and Literature Review
authors: Alina Pietryszyn-Bilińska 1*; Alicja Podolska 2; Magdalena Moś 2; Aleksandra Kawczyk-Krupka 1
journal: International Journal of Clinical Case Reports and Reviews
abstract: Background: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA) is characterised by a thickened aortic wall and periaortic fibrosis. A subset of cases may be associated with IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). We describe diagnostic and management challenges in a patient with IAAA and suspected IgG4-RD. Case presentation: A 62-year-old patient with a history of smoking and contrast-induced nephropathy underwent ultrasonography, computed tomography angiography and laboratory testing, including inflammatory markers and immunological assays. Clinical findings: The abdominal aorta measured 38 mm in diameter, with extensive periaortic inflammatory tissue and approximately 91% cross-sectional area stenosis of the left renal artery on CT angiography. ESR was 52 mm/h and CRP was 17 mg/L; serum IgG4 was reported as elevated, but its numerical value was unavailable. Blood and urine cultures were negative. IgG4-RD was suspected but not histologically confirmed. Prednisone 20 mg/day and lercanidipine 20 mg/day were initiated; blood pressure subsequently measured 110/80 mmHg. Long-term treatment response was not documented. Conclusions: IgG4-RD should be considered among the possible causes of IAAA with extensive periaortic fibrosis. Elevated serum IgG4 alone does not establish the diagnosis. Multidisciplinary evaluation, careful exclusion of infection and serial imaging are important, particularly when operative treatment is considered high risk.

title: Acute decompensated aortic stenosis: the final common pathway of a failing system
authors: Jonathan Vibhishanan; ADRIAN P BANNING; Thomas J. Cahill
journal: European Heart Journal - Valvular and Structural Heart Disease
abstract: Abstract The theoretical paradigm for management of aortic stenosis (AS) assumes an early diagnosis, with surveillance until symptoms develop, followed by an elective intervention. In current practice, however, acute decompensation of aortic stenosis (ADAS) leading to hospital admission is commonplace, and one quarter of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures performed in the UK are now performed urgently on patients with ADAS. Acute decompensation and hospital admission often reflects a failure of the upstream AS pathway, typically encompassing late diagnosis, delays to work-up, and challenges with delivery of definitive procedural intervention. Patients presenting with ADAS have a higher prevalence of cardiac damage, frailty, and comorbidities, all of which impact long-term outcome. This Viewpoint reviews the current paradigm and its limitations, before considering strategies to reduce the frequency of ADAS, and outlining clinical and research priorities to better understand ADAS, to provide better standardisation of care pathways in ADAS, and to improve outcomes for patients that present with ADAS.

title: Evaluation of psychosocial benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients
authors: Vipin Chandra; Ramakant Dixit; Manudev Mehta; Mukesh Goyal
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with significant symptom burden, impaired quality of life, and psychosocial morbidity. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a recommended non-pharmacological intervention, but evidence focusing on its psychosocial benefits remains limited. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of hospital-based outpatient PR on psychosocial parameters and health-related quality of life in patients with COPD receiving standard pharmacotherapy. This before-after interventional study included 50 male patients with stable COPD who underwent a structured outpatient PR program for 24 weeks in addition to standard medical therapy. Assessments were performed at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks. Psychosocial outcomes were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and quality of life was assessed using the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) and the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire-COPD-specific version (SGRQ-C). Statistical analysis was performed with significance set at p<0.05. PR led to significant improvements in psychosocial and quality-of-life outcomes. Mean HADS anxiety and depression scores showed significant reductions at 12 and 24 weeks compared to baseline (p<0.001). Quality-of-life scores improved significantly, with reductions in CAT and SGRQ-C scores at follow-up (p<0.001). A marked reduction in COPD exacerbations and hospital admissions was also observed during the study period. Hospital-based outpatient PR significantly improves psychosocial well-being and health-related quality of life while reducing morbidity in patients with COPD, supporting its routine integration into comprehensive COPD care.

title: Feasibility and safety of early bedside personalized rehabilitation in acute decompensated heart failure: a pilot randomized trial
authors: Puhua Zhang; Xian-Jun Luo; Nuo-Nan Li; Wen-Yin Huang; Zhenzhen Jiang; Hong-Wen Zhu; Xiaoyong Zhu
abstract: The initiation of individualized bedside rehabilitation during the acute phase of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), particularly among elderly patients, remains insufficiently understood. Although early rehabilitation may improve mobility, alleviate congestion, and enhance quality of life (QoL), evidence supporting its effectiveness is limited. To assess the feasibility and safety of early individualized bedside rehabilitation and to explore preliminary between-group differences in physical function and congestion-related outcomes in elderly patients with ADHF prior to discharge. A single-center randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted at the CICU of Jiujiang University Affiliated Hospital from January 2024 to March 2025. Patients aged ≥ 65 years with ADHF were randomly allocated to either the intervention group (IG) or the control group (CG). The IG received early individualized rehabilitation, including mobilization, respiratory training, and low-intensity resistance exercises, whereas the CG received standard conventional treatment. A total of 58 patients were enrolled. The predefined AHF-CR intervention was successfully delivered in all patients allocated to the intervention group (29/29, 100%), and no rehabilitation-related adverse events were observed. Exploratory analyses showed higher SPPB scores in the intervention group at discharge. Early individualized bedside rehabilitation appears to be feasible and safe for elderly patients with ADHF. Preliminary exploratory differences in discharge SPPB and ERCS scores were observed between groups, warranting confirmation in larger adequately powered trials.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Electrocardiography and Immunological Markers (IL-6, TNF-α, and C-Reactive Protein) in the Diagnosis of Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Using Echocardiography as the Gold Standard
authors: Hameed A. Alhibaly; Basama Edan Kadum; Ban Waheed Hussein Bdair; Satar Jabbar Rahi Algraittee; Abdul Amir H. Kadhum
abstract: Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ECG criteria and inflammatory markers—interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and C-reactive protein (CRP)—in detecting LVH. Materials and Methods: A total of 241 patients with concentric LVH confirmed by ECHO were included and categorised into ECG-positive and ECG-negative groups. Additionally, 50 age-matched controls without LVH were recruited. The diagnostic performance of Sokolow–Lyon, Cornell voltage, and Peguero–Lo Presti ECG criteria was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Serum levels of IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP were analysed across different levels of left ventricular mass index (LVMI). Results: Significant differences were observed between ECG groups in interventricular septal thickness, left ventricular diameter, and LVMI (p < 0.05). ECG criteria demonstrated low sensitivity (10.37%–20.75%) but high specificity (up to 100%), with limited overall accuracy. In contrast, IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP levels were significantly elevated in patients with severe LVH (p < 0.001). Conclusions: ECG criteria show high specificity but limited sensitivity in diagnosing LVH. Elevated inflammatory markers correlate strongly with disease severity, suggesting their potential role in improving diagnostic accuracy.

title: Suspected atrioesophageal fistula complicated by coronary air embolism after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: direct angiographic visualization and catheter aspiration in a case report
authors: Chao Yang; Xiaobin Zeng; Shihai Wang; Chaoju Wang; Jianjun Lan; Yahong Wen; Zaiyong Zheng
abstract: Atrioesophageal fistula is a rare but fatal complication of catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation(AF). It may present with infection, dysphagia or other swallowing-related symptoms, neurologic events, and systemic air embolism; coronary air embolism is even less common. Case summary An 84-year-old woman was admitted with recurrent palpitations lasting 1 h, approximately 1 month after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation and left atrial appendage closure(RFCA & LAAC). On admission, she was in sinus rhythm and had a normal cardiac troponin level. Four hours after admission, she abruptly became unresponsive and developed fever and severe respiratory abnormalities. Electrocardiography subsequently showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated gas in the mid right coronary artery with TIMI 0 distal flow, and catheter aspiration was performed. Computed tomography (CT) of the head and chest revealed gas at multiple sites, including the intracranial compartment, cardiac chambers, and great vessels. Blood cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus and other streptococci. Given the recent left atrial ablation, acute neurologic and myocardial ischemic manifestations, multisite intravascular gas, and bacteremia with organisms associated with the oropharyngeal or gastrointestinal flora, an atrioesophageal fistula complicated by systemic air embolism was strongly suspected. Her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she developed cardiac arrest and died approximately 27 h after admission. Conclusion Atrioesophageal fistula and coronary air embolism should be considered in patients who develop fever, impaired consciousness, or acute ST-segment elevation within several weeks of atrial fibrillation ablation. Coronary angiography can directly visualize intracoronary gas and allow catheter aspiration; however, the certainty of an atrioesophageal fistula diagnosis should remain commensurate with the available imaging evidence.

title: Oculomics using artificial intelligence derived retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular health
authors: Harshal A. Sanghvi; Gurnoor Gill; Jay Patel; Minali Prasad; Najah A. Khan; Vimal Sarup; Shailesh Gupta; Kushagra Katariya; Sanjeev P. Bhavnani
abstract: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from retinal vascular morphology, structural and perfusion imaging, retinal aging, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence models linking retinal biomarkers with cardiovascular risk factors, subclinical disease, clinical events, and cardiorenal and metabolic outcomes. These biomarkers may complement conventional risk assessment, but clinical utility is unproven and integration into cardiovascular digital twins remains conceptual. Prospective validation, standardized acquisition, interoperability, interpretability, and equitable evaluation are required before implementation.

title: Enhancing Scientific Validity by Integrating EHR and Claims Data in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative
authors: Steve Robert Makkar; David Daniel Bogumil; Taylor Estepp; Ayya Keshet; Nathan A. Hotaling; Kristen Hansen; Kenneth R. Gersing; Hythem Sidky; Therese N. Tripler
abstract: Purpose: Accurately capturing a patient's health journey is essential for ensuring the validity of scientific and public health studies. Electronic health records (EHR) and administrative claims are commonly used in healthcare research, albeit separately. Previous research has demonstrated that EHR and claims capture different aspects of patient history and care, potentially introducing bias when used alone. In this study, we leveraged the largest public US EHR resource, the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C), alongside Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) claims data to compare their information coverage and agreement. Methods: We integrated N3C EHR and CMS data to create one cohesive dataset and quantified the proportion of key variables present in EHR alone, CMS alone, and the overlap present in both data sources. Overlap in information coverage was quantified pre- and post-landmark diagnosis of COVID-19. To evaluate the impact of data coverage differences, we conducted a case study evaluating the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on ischemic stroke using both data sources alone and in combination. Results: CMS data helped identify many individuals that were duplicated among EHR identifiers. Examination of the overlap showed that CMS data more completely captured conditions, while EHR data more completely captured medications after COVID-19 diagnosis. Some variables exhibited marked differences over time after landmark COVID-19 diagnosis. Using target trial emulation and self-controlled case series methods, we found that data capture variations altered effect estimates: EHR data alone yielded lower risk of ischemic stroke after vaccination in the target trial emulation (odds ratio 0.47, 95% CI 0.28-0.79), with a smaller, non-significant reduction in the self-controlled case series (incidence rate ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.64-1.02), whereas analyses using CMS data alone or both sources combined yielded estimates close to the null in both designs. Conclusions: Results indicated that when using either a national database combining multiple EHR sources, or CMS claims data alone, patients' medical histories are less completely captured compared to when these data sources are combined. Case study results highlighted the value of combining data sources for not only yielding fuller patient health histories and valid scientific results, but for identifying and explaining biases that may emerge in research studies that rely on a single data source.

title: 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy
authors: Heleen Berdina van der Zwaan; Deborah N. Kalkman; Marjolijn J. Broekman; Annemiek C.C. Evers; Bernardine H. Stegeman; Philippine Kiès; Caroline van der Marel; Judith van der Vloed; Iris C.D. Westendorp; Jerome M J Cornette
abstract: This article contextualises the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for managing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and pregnancy in the Netherlands. The guideline addendum provides additional recommendations for situations where the ESC guidelines may not fully align with Dutch clinical practice. By endorsing the ESC guidelines through this addendum, the Netherlands Society of Cardiology (Nederlandse Vereniging Voor Cardiologie) supports its members in adhering to evidence-based management strategies for CVD and pregnancy.

title: Mosaic RASopathies: comprehensive genetic and clinicopathological analysis for diagnosis and management
authors: Tatiana Belysheva; Tatiana V. Nasedkina; Екатерина Евгеньевна Зеленова; Vera V. Semenova; Natalia Semenova; G. B. Sagoyan; Irina S. Kletskaya; Yana V. Vishnevskaya; Елена Вячеславовна Шарапова; Kristina Kulikova; Pavel Vlasov; Alexandra Botkina; Margarita Belogurova; Marina Yu. Dorofeeva; Тимур Валиев; Светлана Рафаэлевна Варфоломеева
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Introduction Mosaic RASopathies are rare conditions caused by postzygotic mutations arising during embryonic development in genes of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway. They are mainly characterized by a combination of epidermal nevi and extracutaneous manifestations. Distinguishing between different entities can be challenging because of their substantial clinical and genetic overlap. Our aim was to demonstrate the importance of genetic background for accurate diagnosis and further prognostic assessment of disease progression by analyzing genotype–phenotype correlations within this clinical group. Methods The study enrolled 18 patients (10 male and 8 female patients) ranging in age from 1 month to 21 years with congenital craniofacial nevi and variable extracutaneous abnormalities. DNA isolated from peripheral blood leukocytes and affected tissues (nevus and tumor) was analyzed using a targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel covering RAS/MAPK pathway genes, followed by Sanger sequencing. Results Eight patients were diagnosed with Schimmelpenning–Feuerstein–Mims syndrome caused by postzygotic pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS (n = 4) or KRAS (n = 4) genes. Seven patients were clinically diagnosed with phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica (PPK), and mosaic genetic variants were identified in the HRAS (n = 4), KRAS (n = 2), or BRAF (n = 1) genes. In two additional patients with similar phenotypes, somatic mutations in PIK3CA (n = 1) and FGFR2 (n = 1) were identified in affected skin, while in one further case, no clinically significant variant was detected. Discussion We compared the spectrum of extracutaneous anomalies according to the affected gene by combining our data with data from other clinical cases of mosaic RASopathies described in the literature. In summary, 53 cases with HRAS postzygotic variants and 41 cases with KRAS variants were included in the analysis of genotype–phenotype correlations. Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) and malignant tumors were associated with pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS gene, while ophthalmological, neurological, cardiovascular, and renal disorders were more common in KRAS -mutant patients. Conclusion Thus, genetic testing of affected tissue in comparison to normal tissue (peripheral blood) is essential for accurate diagnosis of these mosaic disorders. Consideration of clinical manifestations and the identified genotype–phenotype correlations may further assist in determining prognosis and guiding patient management.

title: The spectrum of cardiovascular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide case-control postmortem study
authors: Jessica L. Fairley; Laura Ross; Elizabeth Davida Paratz; Penelope A McKelvie; Simin Daneshvar; Shereen Oon; Dylan Hansen; Wendy Stevens; André La Gerche; Mandana Nikpour
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine cardiovascular pathology in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) vs. population-based controls, and its association with cause of death. METHODS: A case-control postmortem study was performed in Australia using the National Coronial Information System (2000-2025). SLE/RA cases were identified via keyword/ICD-10 code search. Controls were selected from motor vehicle accident deaths (3:1 ratio). Cardiovascular findings/histology were extracted from autopsy reports. Associations between SLE/RA and cardiovascular findings/outcomes using logistic regression (odds ratios (OR), 95% confidence intervals (CI)). RESULTS: 363 cases (240 RA&123 SLE) and 123 controls of similar age (cases 63y (IQR 53-72), vs. controls 59y (47-73), p=0.166) and sex (female 69% vs. controls 75%, p=0.235) were included. Adjusting for age, sex and BMI, myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR3.66, 95%CI2.00-6.72, p<0.001; RA OR3.96, 95%CI2.37-6.60, p<0.001), myocardial inflammation (SLE OR14.79, 95%CI3.35-65.37, p<0.001; RA OR6.35, 95%CI1.44-28.09, p=0.015) and cardiomegaly (SLE OR5.70, 95%CI2.99-10.86, p<0.001; RA OR3.50, 95%CI2.02-6.08, p<0.001) were more frequent in SLE and RA, as were coronary artery disease (CAD; SLE OR2.46, 95%CI1.34-4.51, p=0.004; RA OR2.56, 95%CI1.54-4.27, p<0.001) and microvascular disease (SLE OR10.28, 95%CI2.28- 46.31; RA OR6.74, 95%CI1.53-29.57, p=0.012). Associations between cardiovascular findings and SLE/RA status were strongest in under-60s, and persisted after adjusting for CAD. Cardiovascular death was associated with myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR2.35, 95%CI1.02-5.43, p=0.045; RA OR3.62, 95%CI1.81-7.27, p<0.001), cardiomegaly (SLE OR3.77, 95%CI1.71-8.27, p=0.001; RA OR2.52, 95%CI1.44-4.43, p=0.001) and CAD (SLE OR4.12, 95%CI1.76-9.66, p=0.001; RA OR12.71, 95%CI6.59-24.49, p<0.001); and microvascular disease (OR5.26, 95%CI1.40-19.77, p=0.014) and valvular pathology (OR2.68, 95%CI1.11-6.43, p=0.028) in SLE only. CONCLUSION: This unique dataset identified increased atherosclerotic, inflammatory and fibrotic cardiovascular disease in SLE and RA, particularly in younger individuals. These pathologies were frequently associated with cardiovascular death.

title: Pre-Anesthetic Venous Excess Ultrasound Score for Predicting Spinal Anesthesia-Induced Hypotension in Geriatric Patients Undergoing Elective Lower Body Surgeries: A Prospective Observational Study
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension (SAIH) complications are still prevalent in 16-33% of cases.Objectives: To assess the correlation between the pre-anesthetic venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading system and the prediction of SAIH in elderly patients, as well as the correlation between internal jugular vein (IJV) measurements and SAIH prediction in geriatric patients.Methods: This prospective observational investigation included 127 patients aged ≥ 65 years at Tanta University Hospitals over one year.All patients were divided into two groups: Group A (n = 56) with no SAIH and Group B (n = 71) with SAIH.A comprehensive evaluation of prominent systemic veins, including hepatic, portal, renal, and internal jugular veins, was performed on all patients.Results: Delta IJV diameter (ΔIJV-D), delta IJV area (ΔIJV-A), and IJV collapsibility index (IJV-CI) were significantly predictive of hypotension.ΔIJV-D showed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.697 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >0.11, with 77.46% sensitivity, 57.14% specificity, 69.62% positive predictive value (PPV), and 66.67% negative predictive value (NPV).ΔIJV-A had an AUC of 0.635 (P=0.009) at a cutoff >0.17, with 78.87% sensitivity, 55.36% specificity, 69.14% PPV, and 67.39% NPV.IJV-CI demonstrated an AUC of 0.739 (P<0.001) at a cutoff >19, with 80.28% sensitivity, 76.79% specificity, 81.43% PPV, and 75.44%NPV.Conclusions: Predictors of SAIH in geriatric patients include the simplicity and noninvasiveness of pre-anesthetic IJV-CI, ΔIJV-A, and ΔIJV-D.In contrast, VExUS did not predict SAIH during perioperative assessment.
